description: Hi! We are Moon Green Base! I'm a curious Grade 8 student who loves exploring science, space, and new ideas. I may not know everything, but I'm always excited to learn and try new things. My mom is my mentor, encouraging me and helping me along the way. This is my first NASA Space Apps Challenge, and I can't wait to see what I can discover! Small team, big curiosity! 🚀
summary:
MOON GREEN BASE is an interactive educational game designed to help children aged 7–12 explore the science and challenges of living on the Moon.
Through five learning topics, science quizzes, interactive missions, and a simulated lunar base management system, players learn about life support, energy, radiation protection, and food production.
The project transforms complex space science concepts into an engaging learning experience. It encourages curiosity, scientific thinking, and decision-making while helping young learners understand the challenges of building a sustainable lunar base.
details:
MOON GREEN BASE is an interactive space science learning game that puts players in the role of lunar explorers and base managers.

The project is organized into five main sections:

  1. LEARN – Players explore five learning topics: Moon Secrets, Sun in Action, Space Radiation, Human Body in Space, and Space Farming.
  2. QUIZ – Players answer multiple-choice science questions and receive feedback and explanations to reinforce their understanding.
  3. MISSIONS – Players face simulated lunar mission scenarios, make decisions, and learn about the consequences of different choices.
  4. MY BASE – Players monitor four essential lunar base resources: Life Support, Power, Radiation Shielding, and Food Production.
  5. CEREMONY – Players review their learning progress and mission achievements and receive a game title based on their performance.

The project was designed using Canva, ChatGPT, Canva Code to create an accessible interactive web-based learning experience.

Its educational simulation connects scientific concepts with practical decision-making. Resource levels and mission outcomes are simplified game mechanics, not real measurements or operational predictions for an actual lunar base.

Our goal is to make space science more accessible to young learners and inspire them to think creatively about future human exploration of the Moon.
